title: New York City, USA
overview: New York City is the most populous city in the United States and a global hub of culture, finance, art, and diversity. Comprising five boroughs, NYC offers something for everyone: world-class museums and Broadway shows, iconic skyline views, diverse neighbourhoods, and an unmatched food scene spanning every cuisine on Earth.
best_time_to_visit: April–June and September–November for mild weather and vibrant street life. December is magical for holiday lights but crowded. July–August is hot and busy.
climate: Humid continental. Hot, humid summers (28–32°C), cold winters (-2–5°C) with occasional snow. Spring and autumn are pleasant with temps 10–22°C.

attractions.name: Central Park
attractions.description: 843-acre urban park in the heart of Manhattan. Rent a bike, visit the zoo, or catch a free Shakespeare in the Park performance in summer.

attractions.name: Metropolitan Museum of Art
attractions.description: One of the world's largest and finest art museums with over 2 million works spanning 5,000 years. Pay-what-you-wish for NY state residents.

attractions.name: Statue of Liberty & Ellis Island
attractions.description: Take a ferry from Battery Park to visit America's most iconic landmark and the immigration museum. Book pedestal access well in advance.

attractions.name: Brooklyn Bridge Walk
attractions.description: Walk across the iconic suspension bridge for stunning views of the Manhattan skyline. Free and best in early morning before crowds.

attractions.name: High Line
attractions.description: Elevated linear park built on a former freight rail line on Manhattan's west side. Features gardens, art installations, and great views.

attractions.name: Times Square
attractions.description: The neon-lit heart of Midtown Manhattan. Best experienced at night. Skip the chain restaurants and explore nearby Hell's Kitchen for better food.

attractions.name: One World Observatory
attractions.description: Observation deck atop One World Trade Center with 360° views from 100 floors up. Book online for discounts.

attractions.name: MoMA
attractions.description: Museum of Modern Art with works by Picasso, Pollock, Warhol, and Monet's Water Lilies. Free Friday evenings 5:30–9pm.

food.name: NYC Pizza Slice
food.description: Grab a classic New York dollar slice (now ~$3) and fold it in half. Joe's Pizza in Greenwich Village is the gold standard.

food.name: Bagel & Lox
food.description: Breakfast institution. Ess-a-Bagel and Russ & Daughters on the Lower East Side are legendary. Get it with cream cheese and smoked salmon.

food.name: Smash Burgers at J.G. Melon
food.description: Classic Upper East Side institution for juicy burgers and cottage fries. Cash only.

food.name: Chelsea Market Food Hall
food.description: Former factory building turned gourmet food hall with artisan vendors. Great for a self-guided food tour.

food.name: Katz's Delicatessen
food.description: Iconic Lower East Side Jewish deli, famous for pastrami sandwiches since 1888. A cultural institution as much as a restaurant.

transport: NYC's subway runs 24/7 and is the best way to get around. Single ride $2.90 or get an OMNY-linked unlimited card. For outer boroughs, use the subway + occasional Uber/Lyft. Yellow cabs are plentiful. Walking is often fastest in Midtown.

budget_guide.notes: NYC is expensive. Budget 20% extra for tipping (15–20% on food and services). Many free attractions (Central Park, High Line, Brooklyn Bridge) make budget travel feasible.

tips: Tip 18–20% at restaurants – service charge is rarely included.
Avoid tourist-trap restaurants in Times Square – walk 2 blocks for much better food at lower prices.
The subway is safe and efficient – don't be intimidated by its complexity.
Many world-class museums have suggested (not mandatory) admission – you can pay less.
Visit the Brooklyn side of the Brooklyn Bridge for the best Manhattan skyline photos.
